Decodes an X-address into its XRP classic address and tag.

An X-address packs an XRP classic address and a destination tag into one string. Use this endpoint when someone
gives you an X-address and you need the classic address and the tag separately, for example to show them to a

get.description:
Encodes an XRP classic address and a tag into an X-address.

On the XRP Ledger, many deposit addresses are shared, and the destination tag tells the receiver which account a
payment is for. An X-address packs the classic address and the tag into one string, so a sender cannot leave out
the tag. Use this endpoint to give your users one X-address to send to instead of an address and a separate tag.

The X-address starts with `X` on `mainnet` and with `T` on `testnet`. To split an X-address back into its parts,
use [Decode XRP Address](/api/assets-addresses/decode-xrp-address).

`context` is an optional value of your own that Vaultody returns unchanged in the response, so you can match
responses to requests.

post.description:
Generates an additional receiving/deposit address for a Vault Account on the given blockchain and network.

Use this endpoint when a Vault Account needs more than one address for a chain. For the first address, add the
asset instead with [Add Asset to Vault Account](/api/vault-accounts/add-asset-to-vault-account): that call

are not credited. Add every asset you expect to receive with
[Add Asset to Vault Account](/api/vault-accounts/add-asset-to-vault-account), passing the new `address`, before
you share the address. On UTXO blockchains such as Bitcoin, the native coin is added automatically.

post.description:
Manages TRX staking for one Tron address in a Vault: freeze, unfreeze and withdraw TRX, and delegate bandwidth or energy to other addresses.

Stake TRX to obtain bandwidth or energy, so the address can pay for its transactions with resources instead of
burned TRX. Set `type` to the operation you need:

- `freeze` stakes `amount` TRX for the `resource` you choose.
- `unfreeze` unstakes `amount` TRX. The TRX becomes withdrawable after Tron's waiting period.
- `withdraw-resource` moves unstaked TRX that has passed the waiting period back to the available balance. It
  takes no `amount`.
- `delegate` gives the bandwidth or energy of `amount` staked TRX to `toAddress`. Set `lock` and `lockPeriod` to
  stop the delegation from being cancelled for a while.
- `undelegate` takes delegated resources back from `toAddress`.

The call creates a transaction request from `fromAddress`. Like any outgoing transaction, it goes through your
approval policy before it is signed and broadcast, and you can follow it with
[webhook events](/webhooks/events). Check the result with
[Tron Resource Overview](/api/assets-addresses/tron-resource-overview).

`context` is an optional value of your own that Vaultody returns unchanged in the response, so you can match
responses to requests.

get.description:
Retrieves an overview of TRX staking and resource allocation for one Tron address: the TRX balance, staked TRX, and the bandwidth and energy the address has.

On Tron, every transaction uses bandwidth, and smart contract calls such as TRC-20 transfers also use energy.
An address gets them by staking (freezing) TRX or from another address that delegates them; when it runs out,
the network burns TRX to pay instead. Use this endpoint to monitor your staking and to check that an address
has enough bandwidth and energy before you send from it.

To freeze, unfreeze, withdraw or delegate TRX, use
[Tron Resource Management](/api/assets-addresses/tron-resource-management).

`context` is an optional value of your own that Vaultody returns unchanged in the response, so you can match
responses to requests.

post.description:
Creates one transaction request that sends several asset transfers from a single sender, with a designated fee payer covering the fee.

Creates a batch transaction request that groups multiple asset transfers into a single transaction. The
batch supports multiple recipient transfers initiated from a single sender and sponsored by a
designated fee payer, so all operations execute atomically. On the supported EVM blockchains —
Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain, Optimism, Base, Arbitrum and Polygon — batching uses an EIP-7702-compliant
transaction. On Solana the transfers are batched as a single multi-instruction transaction.

The optional `context` value you send comes back unchanged in the response, so you can match each response
to its request.

post.description:
Calculates an approximate fee for a planned transaction before it is submitted, by the asset you send.

Use it to estimate the cost of a transaction and check that it is feasible before you create it. It
supports every transaction type: single transfer, multiple transfer, Gas Sponsorship, batch transfer and
Tron contract interaction. Set `transactionType` to the type you plan to create (a Gas Sponsorship transfer
uses `single` with a `feePayer`) and send the fields that type needs.

`feePayer` and `feePayerAssetId` are plain strings in `item`, not the nested `feePayer` object of
[Create Batch Transaction Request](/api/transactions/create-batch-transaction-request).

Nothing is created, so you can call it as often as you need. The optional `context` value you send comes
back unchanged in the response, so you can match each response to its request.

Use it before [Create UTXO Transfer](/api/transactions/create-utxo-transfer) to check the senders,

If the Vault Account has no address yet for that asset's blockchain and network, this endpoint derives one and
returns it: pass `label` for that case. Pass `address` instead to add the asset to an address the Vault

get.description:
Returns your Vaults of one type, test or main, with each Vault's ID, name, color, backup status and address counts, one page at a time.

Use it to find the `vaultId` that most other calls take in their path. Vaults are created in the Dashboard;
pass `test` for the Vaults that work on test networks and `main` for the ones that work on main networks.

The list is paginated: pass the `id` of the last Vault on a page as `startingAfter` to get the next page, and
stop when `hasMore` is `false`. See [Rate Limits and Pagination](/get-started/rate-limits-and-pagination).

`context` is an optional value of your own that Vaultody returns unchanged in the response, so you can match
responses to requests.
